items.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns as CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief
items.summary: Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as President, CEO and board member effective November 11, 2026, appointing CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor, and naming Harvey C. Jones as the company's first-ever independent Board Chair. The abrupt leadership change at the world's most valuable chipmaker comes days before its Q3 FY2027 earnings report.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO several times oversubscribed ahead of Nasdaq debut
items.summary: Orders for Anthropic's 825 million IPO shares, priced at $70-$78 each, are reportedly running several times over the amount on offer, with pricing expected November 18 and trading under ticker 'ANT' to begin November 19. A concurrent $26 billion private placement from Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and other partners underscores how central Anthropic has become to AI infrastructure spending.

items.headline: OpenAI closes $11 billion first tranche of new round at $1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: Bloomberg reports OpenAI has wired an initial $11 billion as the first close of a larger funding round, anchored by SoftBank, MGX, Coatue and a UAE-based syndicate, at a valuation of about $1.25 trillion — below the $1.4-1.5 trillion the company had initially sought. The scaled-back figure signals some investor caution even as AI infrastructure spending keeps accelerating.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, low-cost coding and agent model
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, positioned for everyday coding and agentic tasks, claiming it runs some workloads 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash while adding a new 'xhigh' thinking-effort setting. It's rolling out immediately in Google AI Studio, the Gemini app, Search and Google Antigravity, priced at $1.50 per million tokens.

items.headline: IBM and Microsoft launch Imagine Enterprise, a joint AI agent platform
items.summary: IBM and Microsoft unveiled Imagine Enterprise, a jointly built platform for creating, running and governing AI agents for industry-specific workflows, seeded by IBM's library of more than 6,000 pre-built agents and assets on Microsoft's AI and cloud stack. It launches first for financial services, insurance and retail, with manufacturing, energy, public sector and mobility to follow.

items.headline: Nvidia unveils GR00T 2 robotics foundation model and Isaac Lab 3.0 at CoRL
items.summary: At the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, Nvidia introduced GR00T 2, an open 'world action model' built on its Cosmos platform that aims to let robots learn delicate manipulation skills directly from human video, alongside Isaac Lab 3.0 and new open robotics benchmarks. Nvidia hasn't yet specified when the weights will be broadly available, with one report pointing to a December target.

items.headline: Alibaba teases Qwen4, opens a time-limited Qwen4-Max preview
items.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team announced that its next-generation Qwen4 model family is coming soon and opened a free preview of Qwen4-Max with a 1-million-token context window, available through November 25 via its Token Plan, Qoder, QwenWork and other access points. The company has not yet published benchmarks or a model card for the new generation.

items.headline: Embodied AI unveils AIR, a humanoid robot that learns factory tasks on the job
items.summary: Swiss startup Embodied AI showed off AIR, a tendon-driven humanoid robot designed to pick up new factory tasks by watching human demonstrations rather than requiring hand-coded programming, at Humanoid Europe 2026. The launch adds to a crowded field of companies racing to get humanoids onto real production lines rather than just demo stages.

items.headline: Global humanoid robotics race intensifies as Unitree holds market lead
items.summary: A roundup of the fast-growing humanoid robot industry puts China's Unitree in the lead with roughly 31% market share, ahead of rivals like UBTECH and AiMOGA, as manufacturers increasingly compete on real-world deployment rather than demos. The piece frames 2026 as the year physical AI shifted from research showcases toward commercial rollout.

items.headline: New survey questions whether interpretability research is actually making AI safer
items.summary: A large survey posted to arXiv by researchers including Yoshua Bengio, Stella Biderman and Mor Geva reviews the state of mechanistic interpretability for AI safety, concluding that the tools are improving but turning readable explanations of model internals into dependable safety guarantees remains unsolved. The authors flag a 'proxy fidelity problem': how closely an interpretable explanation actually tracks what a model is doing.

items.headline: Mistral AI announces new push for European AI sovereignty
items.summary: Mistral unveiled new initiatives aimed at strengthening European control over AI infrastructure, including expanded local deployment options, broader model access and commitments to long-term European compute capacity, building on its October release of the open-weight, trillion-parameter Mistral Large 4. The moves position Mistral as Europe's standard-bearer against US and Chinese AI labs.

items.headline: Amazon escalates legal fight with Perplexity over its Comet AI shopping agent
items.summary: Amazon formally opposed Perplexity's motion to dismiss US litigation over Comet, Perplexity's AI browser agent that shops on Amazon's site on users' behalf, arguing Perplexity is trying to conceal how the agent operates. The dispute, which earlier saw a preliminary injunction against Perplexity vacated on appeal, highlights growing friction between retailers and AI agents that act as autonomous shoppers.
